meta.title: The Notebook of Repairs That Failed
meta.skill_frame: Find the main idea: decide what a whole passage is mostly about, not one true detail.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is two records, and an idea stated only in the last two sentences. Measured FK 5.9-6.5 on the three parts (Flesch-Kincaid, approximate syllable count). The load sits inside the grade 4-5 band and climbs one knob at a time across the rung: clue distance, then competing details, then how far the idea sits from words the passage uses.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for main_idea 4.1, sequence 6. No external work.
source.survey: The band's ceiling: the first two parts describe two records without ranking them, and the central idea depends on the contrast the last part draws.
source.avoided: No named repair cafe, no brand names, no part numbers.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance, competing details, and distance between the idea and the words.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 75-79 words instead of 100-200. The rung's ceiling lesson keeps three short parts so the contrast between the two records stays in view; the passage totals 230 words over 12 minutes. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The repair cafe opens in a church hall on the first Saturday of the month. People bring lamps, radios, kettles, and once a riding mower. Volunteers with soldering irons sit at long tables and try to fix what comes in. Nobody takes minutes at the tables. For two years the group kept one record: a list of the machines it had fixed, with a total at the bottom. The list was used in a grant application and nowhere else.
passage.part_2: Then a volunteer started a second notebook for the machines that could not be fixed. Each line gave the model, the fault, what was tried, and why it failed. Some cases could not be opened without breaking them. Some needed a part that is no longer made. Some had a battery sealed inside. The glue never held when that case was closed again. After a year, the volunteers read the notebook before they opened anything.
passage.part_3: The notebook changed the work in two ways. Volunteers stopped spending an hour on machines the group had already failed to open. They also began telling a visitor at the door what was likely, before the visitor waited. In the year after the notebook started, the share of machines fixed rose from half to two thirds. That was the group's best year. The list of successes never taught the group anything. The record of failures did.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. So they would not spend an hour repeating a fix that had already failed.

if_they_say.ask: The notebook is about failures. What can a failed repair tell them?

items.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. A repair group began recording its failures, and that record taught it more than its list of successes.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Part one is the list of successes, part two the notebook of failures, part three the two changes and the rise in the share fixed.
tutor_only.tell: The passage is about a repair group that started writing down what it could not fix, and learned more from those notes than from its count of successes.
help: The last two sentences of the passage state the idea. Read them again.
Part one and part two each describe a record. Which one changed the work?
tutor_only.core_idea: A repair group started recording its failures, and that record taught it more than its list of successes did.
accept_ideas: recording failures taught the group more than recording successes
the notebook of failures made them better
writing down what failed helped the group
failures taught them more than successes

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about a list of fixed machines
if_they_say.ask: That list is one part, and the passage says it taught nothing. What did?

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about batteries sealed inside
if_they_say.ask: That is one kind of failure. What did the notebook of failures do for the group?

items.prompt: The passage says the list of successes never taught the group anything. Why not?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The successes only said what already worked; the failures said what to stop trying and what to tell a visitor.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Part three ties the notebook to two changes in practice and a rise in the share of machines fixed, from half to two thirds.
tutor_only.tell: A fixed machine told them the repair worked. A failure told them what not to try, and what to say at the door before a visitor waited.
help: Compare what a success tells a volunteer with what a failure tells them.
Part three names two changes in practice.
tutor_only.core_idea: The successes only confirmed what worked, while the failures told them what to stop trying and what to tell a visitor.

the failures showed what not to try

if_they_say.ask: It was written down and used in a grant application. Why did it teach nothing?
